o: Recall the essential ideas of trace tables.
c: A trace records program state after each instruction that changes a variable.
An accumulator holds a running total; it changes each time a value is added.
Trace iteration counters, condition outcomes and updated values; do not record an update when a branch is skipped.
The final displayed result should agree with the last recorded relevant value.

m.title: Trace Tables · worked example
m.q: Trace total = 0; for i = 1 to 4; total = total + i; next i; print(total). [5 marks]
st: The output is 10; rows record each update to total. [5]

w: Trace total=0; for i=1 to 3; total=total+2; next i. Give each value. [4]
After i=1 total 2 [1], i=2 total 4 [1], i=3 total 6 [1], final output 6 [1].
Trace x=8; if x>5 then x=x-3 endif; print(x). [3]
Condition 8>5 is true [1]; x becomes 5 [1]; output 5 [1].
Explain why trace tables can expose logic errors in a loop. [4]
They show values after each iteration [1], letting a programmer see where an unexpected value appears [1], compare with intended behaviour [1], and locate the faulty update or condition [1].
